title: Isandro and the Debt
premise: Felix Nystrom, a financial-crimes investigator who once infiltrated a laundering network called the Meridian Group, has spent three years burying what he did to survive inside it — including the night his handler, Isandro Vela, died. When a burner phone rings with Isandro's voice, alive and claiming the network faked his death to erase a ledger of everyone they own, Felix is dragged back in as both hunter and suspect. As he follows the money through shell companies toward the network's founder, Felix discovers Isandro's return is itself a test: the ledger exists only if Felix can prove he never stopped being loyal. In the end, Felix burns the network by publishing the ledger himself, choosing truth over the loyalty that was demanded of him — and learns Isandro engineered it all as atonement for the man he made Felix become.
about_author: Odile Sterling is the pen name of a former compliance analyst who spent a decade tracing money across borders before turning to fiction. She writes thrillers about people who know exactly how systems fail because she watched them fail from the inside.

chapters.title: The Clean Money Problem
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Three years after leaving the field, Felix audits spotless accounts for a bank that pays him too well, insomnia-frayed and haunted by the incident he refuses to name. A routine flag on an account leads nowhere — until he recognizes the layering pattern: it's Meridian's signature, updated. Emotional beat: dread resurfacing like a body in water.

chapters.title: Number You Do Not Know
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. A burner phone arrives in his mail with no sender. At 3:07 a.m. it rings, and the voice is Isandro's — the handler who died in front of him. Isandro says one sentence: 'The ledger is still open, and so are you.' Emotional beat: vertigo; grief weaponized into hope.

chapters.title: What the Incident Actually Was
chapters.summary: Felix's POV, intercut with a 2021 flashback. We learn Felix was Meridian's trained insider, and that the night Isandro 'died,' Felix made a choice he's never confessed — he walked away and let it happen. Present-day Felix decides to answer the phone. Emotional beat: guilt sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The First Account
chapters.summary: Dual POV: Felix traces the flagged account while Isandro, in a safehouse, watches him do it. The account belongs to a judge. Isandro feeds Felix one thread of the ledger as bait, testing whether he'll follow the money or report it. Felix follows. Emotional beat: the old intoxication of the work returning, unwelcome.

chapters.title: People Who Own People
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The thread unravels into a web: judges, regulators, two of Felix's current colleagues. His supervisor, Dana Okafor, notices his queries and quietly warns him someone upstairs asked about them first. Emotional beat: paranoia — every ally now reads as surveillance.

chapters.title: The Man Who Trains Them
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Flashback chapters reveal Meridian's founder, Aurel Sartorius, who recruits broken people and rebuilds them loyal. Isandro confesses (to us, not Felix) that faking his death was Sartorius's order — and that surviving it broke his obedience. Emotional beat: the corrupter corrupted by conscience.

chapters.title: Dead Drop, Live Wire
chapters.summary: Felix and Isandro meet in person for the first time in three years, in a ferry terminal. It goes wrong: Meridian's cleaners were expecting the meeting, meaning someone leaked it. They escape separately; Felix realizes only three people knew. Emotional beat: betrayal closing in from inside the alliance.

chapters.title: Dana
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Confronting Dana, Felix finds she isn't the leak — she's been running her own quiet investigation since her brother was ruined by a Meridian-touched fund. But her files show the leak's identity: Isandro's safehouse contact. The test was double-blind. Emotional beat: loyalty re-examined as just another control mechanism.

chapters.title: The Ledger and the Knife
chapters.summary: Climax. Felix reaches Sartorius's vault via the banking backdoor Isandro trained him to find — proving the training was always the point. Sartorius offers Felix everything: erasure, wealth, Isandro's real death certificate signed by Felix's own hand. Felix takes the ledger instead, triggering the burn protocol as Sartorius's people close in. Isandro takes a bullet meant for him. Emotional beat: choice made under maximum cost.

chapters.title: Everything Published
chapters.summary: Felix's POV, weeks later. The ledger is public; arrests ripple outward; Felix loses his job, his clearance, his clean money — and sleeps through the night for the first time. He visits Isandro, recovering and finally honest, and forgives neither of them completely. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace; truth outlasting loyalty.
